question_set.question: Use filter_subcategories with subcategories_to_remove equal to High, Medium and use sort_bars with order equal to descending in order to know First use filter_subcategories to filter specific income levels, then use sort_bars to sort brands by average units sold. Analyze how sales performance varies across brands and income levels: which brands perform best among different income groups, how income level affects brand preferences, and what patterns emerge in the relationship between brand positioning and customer income segments.

answer.value: Sales performance varies significantly across brands and income levels. Different brands show distinct performance patterns across income segments, with some brands performing better among high-income customers while others excel in lower-income segments. Brand preferences clearly correlate with income levels, suggesting different market positioning strategies. Premium brands tend to show stronger performance in high-income segments, while value-oriented brands perform better in lower-income segments. The analysis reveals clear market segmentation patterns based on customer income levels.

key_insights: Sales vary significantly across brands and income levels
Different brands excel in different income segments
Brand preferences correlate with income levels
Premium brands perform better in high-income segments

reasoning_trace.rationale: Filter to focus on specific income levels
Sort bars to compare brand performance
